title: Minimize the Maximum Edge Weight of Graph
summary: Given the integers n and threshold, along with a directed weighted graph consisting of n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1, you are to remove some edges from the graph.
statement: Given the integers n and threshold, along with a directed weighted graph consisting of n nodes numbered from 0 to n - 1, you are to remove some edges from the graph. The goal is to ensure that node 0 is reachable from all other nodes, minimize the maximum edge weight in the resulting graph, and ensure that each node has at most threshold outgoing edges. Return the minimum possible value of the maximum edge weight after making the necessary edge removals. If it is impossible to satisfy all conditions, return -1.
constraints: 2 <= n <= 100,000; directed weighted edges have positive weights; threshold is at least one.
Remove edges so every node can reach node zero and each node retains at most threshold outgoing edges.
Minimize the largest retained edge weight, or return -1 when reachability is impossible.
hints: With threshold at least one, a reachable solution can keep one next edge per nonzero node, so the degree cap does not change feasibility.
Binary-search a weight limit and traverse reversed eligible edges from zero.
Keep edges of weight at most the limit; if reversed reachability visits n nodes, lower the limit.
Reverse reachability is equivalent to every original node reaching zero, and feasibility is monotone in the weight limit.
editorial: Reverse reachability is equivalent to every original node reaching zero, and feasibility is monotone in the weight limit.

tests.explanation: Using only weight-one edges still gives every node a path to zero, so the minimum limit is one.
Node one has no path to zero under any limit, so return -1.
